keyChanges.title: Samsung Taylor Fab fully booked for 2nm before trial ops; AI5/AI6 yield reaches 80%
keyChanges.description: Multiple Korean and semiconductor industry sources (Sept 8–9) report Samsung's Taylor, Texas fab is at full capacity before a single wafer ships. Confirmed 2nm orders: Tesla AI5 and AI6, Broadcom next-gen chips, and Arm edge-AI. Trial operations expected late September or early October 2026; mass production 2027. Monthly capacity 50,000 wafer starts. Samsung 2nm yield improved from ~60% early 2026 to ~80%, crossing the HVM threshold. Critically, 'fully booked' and 'trial operations imminent' does not mean chip delivery: Tesla will not receive production AI5 wafers from Taylor until 2027. TSMC continues to dominate with ~80,000 wsm and a multi-month tape-out head-start. Taylor Fab 2 groundbreaking confirmed for end-2026 with mass production targeting 2030.

positive_signals: Samsung 2nm yield improved from ~60% to ~80% at Taylor, crossing the HVM threshold
Taylor fab fully booked with Tesla AI5 and AI6 orders before opening, removing demand-side risk
Trial operations expected late September or early October 2026
Samsung 2nm order volume projected to more than double in 2026 vs 2025
Taylor Fab 2 groundbreaking confirmed for end-2026
negative_signals: Trial operations ≠ chip delivery: Tesla AI5 production wafers from Taylor not expected until 2027
Samsung lags TSMC on capacity (50K wsm vs ~80K wsm) and overall foundry market share (~7% vs ~73%)
TSMC taped out AI5 months earlier; Samsung version remains a secondary allocation
Taylor Fab 2 mass production not until 2030 — AI6 volume at Taylor is years away
AI5 chip remains pre-volume for vehicles; AI4 is still the in-vehicle standard
80% yield figure comes from industry sources, not official Samsung/Tesla disclosure

keyChanges.title: First-week Cybercab service: 25–45 min waits, software bugs, mid-lane drop-offs
keyChanges.description: The Verge (Sept 9), MotorTrend, and Stick Shifting independently documented consistent service-quality problems in the first full week of public Cybercab rides in Austin. Wait times ranged 25–45 minutes for a 45-car fleet across a 288-sq-mi geofence. Drop-offs occurred mid-lane on busy roads rather than at the curb, causing traffic blockages. Wipers activated on a sunny 95°F day. One rider's touchscreen froze, the car circled aimlessly, and the rider had to exit manually and call a Lyft. Fares were Uber-comparable ($15–21) but one report calculated a $15.85/mile rate versus Waymo's $1.75/mile. Positively, the hardware interior is genuinely impressive. These are first-week field reports from multiple independent journalists, not a single anecdote.

positive_signals: Interior hardware praised across all three reviews: spacious legroom, massive touchscreen, smooth quiet ride
Butterfly doors and automatic open/close well-received in most rides
Price competitive with Uber on a per-trip basis ($15–21)
negative_signals: 45-car fleet generates 25–45 minute wait times for rides under 2 miles
Multiple documented drop-offs mid-lane on busy roads, blocking traffic
Software: wipers on during 95°F sunny day, indecisive lane changes, nervous braking
Frozen touchscreen left one rider with no route display; car stalled, rider had to exit manually
No freeway access, no airport; geofence severely limits utility
Multiple journalists note it feels unfinished, not ready for primary transport use

keyChanges.title: Cybercab open to anyone via app — but 49 Texas-registered units cannot meet public demand
keyChanges.description: Tesla's official @robotaxi account posted September 10 that 'Anyone can try Cybercab in Austin — just download the Robotaxi app & hail a ride,' dropping the invite-only framing. Simultaneously, Texas DMV records showed the registered Cybercab count at 49 — only 4 cars added from the 45 present at launch September 4. Demand clearly exists (Tesla moved the public launch window earlier 'due to popular demand'), but 49 registered Cybercabs across a 288-sq-mi Austin geofence cannot supply the volume that open access implies. Most requests in peak hours result in 25–45 minute waits or no availability.

positive_signals: Official Robotaxi account removes invite-only restriction, opening to general public
Strong demand signal: Tesla moved launch window up 3 hours 'due to popular demand' on Sept 4
Service is live and publicly accessible — a genuine operational milestone
negative_signals: Only 49 Cybercabs registered in Texas as of Sept 10 — just 4 added in 5 days post-launch
25–45 min wait times reported consistently by multiple journalists in the first week
49 cars across 288-sq-mi geofenced city cannot meet open public demand
TxMCCS registration ceiling is not the same as active dispatch count; pool is smaller still

keyChanges.title: Giga Texas ships Cybercabs with factory-integrated Starlink in volume for the first time
keyChanges.description: Drone photographer Joe Tegtmeyer documented September 8 that the Giga Texas outbound lot contained 'many more Cybercabs and for the 1st time equipped with the Starlink module on the hatch in big numbers.' Earlier Starlink-equipped sightings were one-off or retrofit; this is the first aerial confirmation of factory-fit Starlink shipping in volume. Starlink provides satellite connectivity when cellular coverage drops, which matters for unsupervised robotaxi operations. If this becomes standard build spec, all production Cybercabs will ship connectivity-redundant. Production appeared to ramp back up after the Labor Day holiday pause.

positive_signals: Factory-integrated Starlink on Cybercab hatch now shipping in volume — not retrofit
Production restarted and visibly ramped after Labor Day weekend pause
Satellite backup connectivity improves service reliability for unsupervised ops
negative_signals: Single aerial observer source (Tegtmeyer); Tesla has not officially confirmed Starlink as standard
Volume of Cybercabs exiting factory still not quantified — 'many more' is relative
VIN floor is still the Aug 10 estimate of 2,172+ units; no new count available

keyChanges.title: Cybercab Japan Tour opens in Tokyo — static display only, no service launch or regulatory path
keyChanges.description: Tesla Japan launched the 'Cybercab Japan Tour' September 11 at OMAKASE Aoyama Garden in Tokyo, the vehicle's first public showing in Japan. The tour runs through four venues in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya across September. Admission is free with no reservation. This is a static display event — no test rides, no Robotaxi launch announcement, no regulatory pathway for Japan operations. Tesla Japan framed it as 'designed from the ground up for unsupervised taxi use.' Japan has no active Cybercab regulatory process underway.

positive_signals: First public Japan showing signals Tesla is marketing Cybercab for future international markets
Four-city Japan tour (Tokyo Aoyama, Osaka, Nagoya, Tokyo Shinjuku) through late September
negative_signals: Static display only — no rides, no operational launch, no Japan-specific regulatory announcement
Japan has no established Cybercab approval process or timeline
Tour is a marketing event, not an operational milestone

keyChanges.title: Slovenia approves FSD Supervised, becoming 7th consumer market and 6th EU member state
keyChanges.description: Slovenia's Traffic Safety Agency confirmed it recognized the Dutch RDW provisional type approval September 8, 2026, making it the sixth EU member state and seventh global market where Tesla FSD Supervised is legal on public roads. Tesla Europe announced on X: 'FSD Supervised now approved in Slovenia. Rollout will begin soon.' All authorized vehicles must be Hardware 4; drivers must complete a mandatory tutorial and quiz. FSD stays active crossing between approved EU countries, disengaging automatically before entering an unapproved one. Slovenia breaks a three-month approval hiatus since Belgium in June, but its population of ~2.1 million adds negligibly to the ~9% of EU population currently covered by all six approved states.

positive_signals: Official confirmation from Slovenian Traffic Safety Agency via email to Reuters
Slovenian Energy and Infrastructure Minister Vrtovec publicly endorsed the approval
Breaks 3-month approval drought since Belgium in June
Cross-border FSD continuity confirmed between all six approved EU states
negative_signals: Slovenia's 2.1 million population contributes negligibly to the 65% EU population threshold needed for Oct 6 bloc-wide vote
All six approvals rest on one sealed Dutch safety file not reviewable by other member states or the public
Does not bring Tesla closer to Germany (84M), France (68M), or Italy (60M) — required to pass the Oct 6 vote
National cascade of small-population approvals cannot by itself unlock EU-wide authorization

keyChanges.title: EU TCMV October 6 vote faces near-certain failure: 9% coverage, speed-offset deadlock, sealed-file controversy
keyChanges.description: With the October 6 EU Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles vote 28 days away, the structural arithmetic is deeply unfavorable. The six approved countries collectively represent ~42 million people — approximately 9% of the EU's ~450 million population. A qualified majority requires at least 15 member states representing 65% of EU population (~293 million). Without Germany (84M), France (68M), Italy (60M), or Spain (47M) voting yes, the threshold is mathematically unreachable. None of the four has approved FSD nationally, and none has committed to voting yes. Sweden submitted a written no to the TCMV on April 30 unless Tesla removes its speed-offset feature (which allows the car to exceed speed limits by a user-set margin). France has a public reservation on the same feature. Tesla has not removed speed-offset from any EU market. The ETSC has formally asked the European Commission to pause the vote. If the vote fails or defers, existing national approvals remain valid but bloc-wide harmonization slips to early 2027 at the earliest.

positive_signals: October 6 vote is on the calendar; Tesla publicly states it supports proceeding
Six countries already voted yes and will likely vote yes at TCMV
France moved to active UTAC road tests; Finland and Greece considering approvals
Italy's senate saw a formal parliamentary question pushing for FSD approval
negative_signals: Six approved countries = only ~9% of EU population; threshold requires 65% (~293M)
Sweden has a written no on record (April 30) unless speed-offset is removed
France has a public reservation on speed-offset; July safety objections still on record
Germany, Italy, Spain have committed to nothing; none has approved nationally
ETSC formally requested Commission pause the vote pending transparent review
Tesla has not removed speed-offset feature from any EU market
Without Germany or France, even every other EU country cannot reach 65% threshold
Next realistic vote after October 6 if it fails or defers: early 2027

keyChanges.title: All six EU FSD approvals rest on a single sealed Dutch safety file no regulator or citizen can inspect
keyChanges.description: A TechTimes investigation published September 8 confirmed that every one of the six EU national FSD approvals — Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, and Slovenia — derives from a single Dutch RDW provisional type approval file sealed at Tesla's request as a commercial secret. Under EU Regulation 2018/858 Article 39, other member states can recognize the Dutch certification without repeating the technical review, which five countries did without seeing the file. The October 6 TCMV vote, if it passes, would extend this approval to all 27 member states and ~450 million people on the basis of evidence that none of them can read. Multiple EU regulators including Germany, Norway, and Denmark have refused FOIA requests citing trade-secret protections. The ETSC called this a structural gap in EU vehicle type approval regulation. Tesla published a voluntary Article 39 public dashboard September 1 using pre-April 2026 crash data showing a 4.1x safety improvement (reduced from a previously claimed 5.2x), but this does not substitute for the sealed primary approval record.

positive_signals: Tesla published a voluntary public safety dashboard on Sept 1 (Article 39 dashboard)
Dutch RDW conducted 18+ months of independent testing before initial approval in April
Six countries recognized the approval; none has reversed their decision
negative_signals: Dutch safety file sealed at Tesla's request; methodology and conclusions classified as trade secret
Six EU regulators including Germany, Norway, Denmark refused FOIA requests on Tesla's trade-secret grounds
EU-wide vote would ratify approval across 27 states and 450M people without public evidentiary record
ETSC formally requested Commission pause the vote and require transparent, independently verified review
Tesla's public dashboard uses pre-April crash data and shows 4.1x safety ratio, down from claimed 5.2x
EU has no NTSB-equivalent to audit real-world FSD performance independently

keyChanges.title: Germany's KBA confirms active FSD review on EU-wide and national tracks; no approval or timeline given
keyChanges.description: Germany's Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) confirmed September 11, 2026 it is actively reviewing Tesla FSD Supervised for approval along two legal paths under EU Regulation 2018/858 Article 39: the standard TCMV committee procedure (vote expected October 6) and a national exemption route under Article 39(5) allowing Germany to recognize the Dutch RDW provisional type approval unilaterally, as the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, and Slovenia already did. The KBA confirmed receipt of Tesla's application materials and stated it is evaluating traffic safety aspects, including independent on-road testing with a Tesla vehicle. No formal approval, concrete timeline, or decision in favor of the national path has been announced. Germany (84M people, ~19% of EU population) voting yes at the October TCMV meeting — or a national pre-approval — would dramatically reshape the probability of EU-wide authorization passing.

positive_signals: KBA explicitly confirmed it is evaluating both the TCMV route and a national pre-approval route
Germany received a Tesla vehicle for independent on-road testing
German federal government (BMV) views autonomous driving ramp-up as high priority
Article 39(5) national path used successfully by 5 other EU states
negative_signals: KBA confirmed review only; no approval, no timeline, no decision favoring national path announced
KBA has been reviewing the Dutch file since at least May 2026 with no outcome
Germany has previously declined to rush a national approval before EU-wide consensus
FOIA requests for the sealed Dutch safety file refused in Germany
October 6 timeline is extremely tight for a formal German position

keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.9 (2026.27.6) enters public early-access rollout; only 0.2% of fleet after 4 days
keyChanges.description: Tesla began rolling out FSD Supervised v14.3.9 in firmware 2026.27.6 on September 8, 2026, replacing the employee-only 2026.27.5 build. The update includes two branches: HW4 vehicles get v14.3.9 with Automatic Collision Evasion (highway frontal-crash steering maneuver when under 85 mph), a rewritten MLIR-based AI compiler delivering 20% faster reaction time, an upgraded RL training stage, and a new vision encoder for rare/low-visibility scenarios. HW3 Model 3 and Model Y owners receive v14.2 Lite (parking/unparking, Arrival Options, Speed Profiles including new SLOTH profile). As of September 12, TeslaFi shows only 114 cars (0.2% of fleet) on 2026.27.6, while 28.9% of the fleet remains on the previous wide build 2026.26.6.5. FSD v15 is absent from all consumer vehicles.

positive_signals: Automatic Collision Evasion (HW4) is a genuine new safety capability — steering around imminent frontal crashes
MLIR compiler rewrite achieves 20% faster reaction time — a measurable improvement
HW3 Model 3/Y owners receive v14.2 Lite with parking, Arrival Options, Speed Profiles
HW4 and HW3 firmware merged into single build (2026.27.6), reducing fragmentation
negative_signals: Only 0.2% of fleet (114 cars) after 4 days — confined to early access, no wide rollout

keyChanges.title: HW3 Model S/X still missing FSD v14 Lite; Elluswamy says it was 'supposed to go out last week'
keyChanges.description: During the Cybercab launch event in Austin, Tesla AI lead Ashok Elluswamy told IGN's Ryan McCaffrey that FSD v14 Lite for HW3 Model S and Model X was 'supposed to go out last week,' signaling an imminent release. However, the September 8 rollout of 2026.27.6 explicitly lists only 'Models: 3 Y' for FSD v14.2 Lite, leaving HW3 S/X owners without any v14-generation FSD. HW3 Model 3/Y received v14 Lite in late June 2026; S/X HW3 owners have been stuck on the legacy branch since then. NotATeslaApp confirmed that v14 Lite for S/X is 'ready' and expected 'any day now,' but the build has not shipped as of September 12. The Elluswamy statement was secondhand (McCaffrey's recollection) rather than an official Tesla communication.

positive_signals: Elluswamy reportedly confirmed the S/X v14 Lite build is ready and expected to ship very soon
HW3 Model 3/Y has already proven v14 Lite architecture works on legacy hardware

HW3 S/X owners have been excluded from v14 Lite for 2+ months while 3/Y owners received it
No official Tesla announcement or timeline — only a secondhand conference hallway quote
HW3 S/X owners are off the unsupervised FSD roadmap regardless; Lite ceiling is permanent without HW upgrade

keyChanges.title: Elluswamy previews FSD v15 safety promise; v15 carries no consumer release date
keyChanges.description: On September 11, 2026, Tesla AI lead Ashok Elluswamy responded to a near-miss incident shared by an owner, writing: 'Glad you are safe. Even earlier prediction of hazards, even faster reaction time and overall significantly better safety and collision avoidance coming as part of the next big upgrade (v15).' Teslarati contextualized this against Tesla's published FSD safety data: FSD vehicles travel 5.1–5.7 million miles between airbag-deployment events vs. ~699,000 miles for the U.S. average (Tesla's preferred comparison), but the same-car baseline shows a narrower 2.4–2.7x advantage. v15 remains absent from all consumer vehicles. The previously reported target of end-2026 / early 2027 has not changed. Robotaxi builds using early v15 are operational in Austin but inaccessible to consumer hardware. The Elluswamy tweet is a product promise tied to no verified code drop or OTA timeline.

positive_signals: Elluswamy confirms v15 is targeting hazard prediction, reaction time, and collision avoidance
Early v15 builds reportedly running in Austin robotaxi fleet with ~40% of planned improvements in internal benchmarks
FSD safety data shows measurable advantage vs. U.S. average (5.1–5.7M miles per airbag event vs. 699K)

FSD same-car safety comparison shows a narrower 2.4–2.7x advantage, not the advertised 7x vs. U.S. average
HW3 vehicles confirmed off the v15 roadmap entirely; HW4 sufficiency for 10B-parameter model still a promise

keyChanges.title: Optimus Production Associate listing expires Sept 8 — production-scale hiring absent for 7+ weeks
keyChanges.description: The only Production Associate, Optimus posting (Fremont, originally listed Jul 24, 2026 at $25.76–$34.68/hr) was removed from job boards around September 8, 2026 — confirmed via iHireManufacturing showing 'removed 4 days ago' as of September 12. No new production-associate or floor-operator replacement appeared during the September 6–12 window. Engineering, technician, and AI roles continue to appear, but the single metric that directly signals readiness to hire hourly assembly workers for a production ramp has disappeared without replacement for the second consecutive research cycle. Without production associates, no meaningful volume ramp is possible regardless of engineer headcount.

positive_signals: Production Associate hiring did exist briefly (Jul 24 listing), showing the role was opened at some point
Multiple engineering and technician roles for Optimus manufacturing still active
negative_signals: Production Associate, Optimus (Fremont) listed Jul 24, expired ~Sept 8 with no replacement
Two consecutive research cycles show zero active Production Associate, Optimus listings
Without production associates (the actual assembly workers), no volume ramp is possible
Q2 2026 earnings confirmed 'no production figure given' and initial builds go to internal Optimus Academy — hiring pattern consistent with prototype-scale output

keyChanges.title: Tesla Langley BC Optimus actuator/geartrain cluster grows to 12+ roles — supply chain broadening signal
keyChanges.description: A September 9, 2026 Active Vancouver article confirmed Tesla's Langley, British Columbia facility has grown from a single Canadian Optimus posting to more than a dozen roles covering Robotics Manufacturing Engineer (Line Design, Geartrain), Robotics Engineering Technician (Metrology), Robotics Technical Project Manager (Actuator Manufacturing), and geartrain equipment engineers. Compensation ranges from $23.41/hr for technicians to C$207,900/yr for senior geartrain engineers. The cluster is focused on actuator gearbox production, indicating Tesla is building in-house actuator supply chain capability in Canada, not just Austin. However, the underlying job postings originate from May–June 2026; the article is a new synthesis published in-window. This is a positive hiring-breadth signal but does not indicate a near-term production ramp.

positive_signals: Tesla Langley BC now has 12+ Optimus roles spanning manufacturing, controls, metrology, and test engineering
In-house actuator/geartrain manufacturing in Canada diversifies supply chain beyond Austin and Fremont
Salary ranges ($120k–$207k CAD for senior roles) indicate serious investment, not exploratory hiring

keyChanges.title: Jiemian reports Tesla placed first batch order for ~5,000 Optimus components with T-chain suppliers
keyChanges.description: Jiemian News, citing channel checks within Tesla's core manufacturing network, reported September 7, 2026 that Tesla placed bulk purchase orders for approximately 5,000 units' worth of components with T-chain suppliers. This marks the first thousand-unit-scale procurement order after only a few hundred units in earlier pilot runs. Fremont humanoid assembly line underwent initial equipment debugging starting in July, completing preliminary trial phases by mid-August; yield improvements were the stated prerequisite for releasing this commercial-grade parts order. Internal 2026 target: 10,000–20,000 units for internal deployment. Supplier capacity ramp targets: 1,000 units/week by end of September, 2,000–2,500/week by year-end. Tesla has not officially confirmed these purchase orders. As of the August 20 JPMorgan Fremont visit, the Optimus area was still tarped off with no robots working on the floor. Gen 3 has not been publicly unveiled. Commercial external sales remain 'as early as H2 2027.'

keyChanges.title: China August retail confirmed at 50,047 — down 12.43% YoY, weakest August since 2022, Model Y falls 26%
keyChanges.description: CPCA published August 2026 market data September 8, printing the China retail figure that was unresolved last week. Tesla sold 50,047 vehicles in China retail in August, down 12.43% year-over-year and marking the third consecutive annual decline in monthly retail sales — the weakest August performance since 2022. The MoM bounce (+83.67% from July's 27,249) reflects the predictable end-of-quarter trough pattern but does not reverse the YoY trajectory. Model Y specifically fell 25.76% YoY to 29,260 units, deepening from -18.23% in July and -13.81% in June (third consecutive monthly YoY decline). Model 3 rose 17.18% YoY to 20,787 — the highest of 2026 — but at insufficient volume to offset Model Y's decline. YTD China retail: 316,251 through August, down 12.44% YoY. Tesla held 7.17% of China BEV market share vs. 8.33% a year earlier. Giga Shanghai exports of 36,119 (down 45.55% MoM but up 38.71% YoY) confirm the factory is prioritizing export markets over domestic demand.

Model 3 deliveries up 17.18% YoY to 20,787, highest monthly total of 2026
Exports up 38.71% YoY, showing Shanghai continues to supply global markets

keyChanges.title: Tesla China launches Q3 inventory incentives: 10,000 yuan off Model Y, 5,000 yuan off Model 3
keyChanges.description: Tesla China announced September 7 that customers ordering and taking delivery of in-stock vehicles by September 30 receive cash reductions of 5,000 yuan on Model 3 and 10,000 yuan on all Model Y inventory variants (including Model Y L and the new Performance). Combined with 5-year 0% financing and an 8,000 yuan paint benefit on select configs, effective starting prices drop to historic lows: Model 3 from 222,500 yuan (~$33,000) and Model Y from 253,500 yuan (~$38,000). The promotion drew a surge in orders but triggered owner backlash — existing buyers who took delivery before September 7 cannot retroactively claim the discount. Background: Giga Shanghai hit a first-half 2026 output record, creating inventory surplus as China domestic retail fell 12.44% YTD. The incentive is a tactical volume pull-forward for Q3, not a permanent price cut.

Covers full Model Y lineup including new Performance and Model Y L

keyChanges.title: Tesla Model Y Performance launches in China at 369,000 yuan — completes Juniper lineup as YoY sales weaken
keyChanges.description: Tesla opened Model Y Performance ordering in China September 11, 2026 at 369,000 yuan (~$54,450). The Shanghai-built, dual-motor variant is the fifth Model Y configuration in China and the most expensive. Specs: 3.5s 0-100 km/h, 250 km/h top speed, 659 km CLTC range, 250 kW fast charge. Delivery window: 2-6 weeks. The launch arrives as Model Y China deliveries have fallen 25.76% YoY in August (third consecutive monthly decline). The Performance is a margin and mix story — ASP uplift of 100,500 yuan above base Model Y — rather than a volume driver. By comparison, BYD's flash charging covers 500 km in 10 minutes vs. Tesla's 250 km in 15 minutes at this price tier.

2-6 week delivery window suggests Tesla has production ready

keyChanges.title: Giga Berlin orders three extra shifts targeting 7,500 vehicles/week for Q3 push — still short of target
keyChanges.description: Tesla ordered three mandatory extra production shifts at Gigafactory Berlin in September 2026 to push output toward 7,500 vehicles per week by mid-October, per a September 7 report. Current production sits around 6,500 vehicles/week, up from ~5,000/week in June after plant manager André Thierig set the 7,500 target. The extra shifts: night shift September 18, early shift September 19, night shift September 25. Each of Giga Berlin's three shift groups will be called in once; workers receive a 35% surcharge. Even with extra shifts, Tesla expects peak-week output of 7,100–7,300 vehicles — still short of the 7,500 goal. Context: Germany August registrations were 3,034, up 110.5% YoY; but Europe Q3 QTD registrations track at record lows (-37.5% YoY through August) with 2 of 3 months complete.

Germany registrations up 110.5% YoY in August; YTD +182%
Extra shifts demonstrate Tesla is actively pushing Q3 European production volumes

keyChanges.title: Cybertruck + Powerwall 3 Powershare integration goes live — 3+ days of home backup, Powerwall 2 still pending
keyChanges.description: Tesla enabled Powershare + Powerwall 3 integration via OTA on September 10, 2026, allowing Cybertruck owners to pair the truck with an existing Powerwall 3 for combined home backup extending over 3 days — equivalent to 9 additional Powerwalls, per Tesla's official Cybertruck account. Lead engineer Wes Morrill confirmed the rollout and called it the first vehicle-home battery joint operation of this kind. Powershare itself launched with Cybertruck in November 2023; basic home backup via a Gateway arrived in 2024. The missing piece — making Powershare work alongside a Powerwall rather than as a competing backup source — required certifying two grid-forming devices negotiating grid management across multiple Powerwall hardware generations. The feature was originally promised for 2025, then pushed to mid-2026. Powerwall 2 and Powerwall+ compatibility is still pending for later in 2026.

3+ days of combined home backup is a meaningful improvement over single-Powerwall capacity
Official Tesla Cybertruck account and lead engineer Wes Morrill both confirmed rollout
Expands Cybertruck's home energy role beyond original Powershare launch capability
negative_signals: Feature was originally promised at Cybertruck launch in November 2023 — arrived nearly 3 years late
Powerwall 2 and Powerwall+ compatibility still pending, limiting reach to Powerwall 3 owners only

keyChanges.title: SpaceX sues Texas AG and Grimes County to block release of Terafab tax-break records
keyChanges.description: SpaceX filed a lawsuit September 9 in Travis County's 126th District Court against Texas AG Ken Paxton and Grimes County to permanently block release of public records related to Terafab's tax-abatement application and negotiation communications. Records were originally requested in May–June 2026 under the Texas Public Information Act. On July 28, Paxton's office ruled most records should be released — allowing only attorney-client communications to remain withheld. Rather than allow release, SpaceX is asserting trade-secret arguments itself in court. SpaceX seeks to shield: the full tax-abatement application, negotiation correspondence, technical and project design information, site-location and land-acquisition records, cost and financial data, and employee contact details. SpaceX also seeks a temporary restraining order blocking release while the case is pending. No judge had ruled as of September 10. GCCRD is considering formally intervening in the case.

negative_signals: Texas AG already ordered most records released — SpaceX is fighting against its own state government to suppress information
